name: Alkort
description: Alkort is a legendary Icelandic partnership game belonging to the ancient Karnöffel family. It is famous for its archaic, bizarre card rankings where Sevens are invincible when led, and the King of Diamonds reigns supreme—unless a Seven is turned against him.

overview.description: Alkort is a legendary Icelandic partnership game belonging to the ancient Karnöffel family. It is famous for its archaic, bizarre card rankings where Sevens are invincible when led, and the King of Diamonds reigns supreme—unless a Seven is turned against him.

history.origins: Part of the oldest surviving family of European card games, Alkort was preserved in the isolation of Iceland for centuries. It shares DNA with the German Karnöffel and Swiss Kaiserspiel.
timeline: 1726-1768: Referenced by Eggert Ólafsson as a native Icelandic pastime.
1880s: Detailed rules published by Ólafur Davíðsson.
1989: Modern Icelandic standard finalized in 'Spilabók AB'.
history.cultural: Regarded as a test of memory and partnership intuition. The term 'Bísefarnir' (Sevens) is a unique Icelandic card-game jargon.
history.evolution: Has changed little since the 18th century, maintaining its complex 'Stock Exchange' rule and the 'Stroke' scoring system.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: 44 cards (52 minus the 10s and 5s). Ace is high, but rankings are non-linear.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives 9 cards to each player in batches of 3. The remaining 8 cards form a face-down stock (hidden).

rules.objective: Win at least 5 tricks (out of 9) to score. Bonus points for 'Múk' (first 5 tricks) or a 'Stroke' (uninterrupted run of tricks).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Showing**: Partners show each other their highest-ranking card before play starts. 2. **Friðufær Check**: If a player has no cards high enough to beat an 8, they can show their hand and swap it for the 8-card stock. 3. **The Trick**: Play is clockwise. There is NO requirement to follow suit. 4. **Ties**: If two cards of equal rank are played (e.g., two Jacks), the first one played wins the trick. 5. **Leading Sevens**: You cannot lead a Seven until you have won at least one trick previously.
keyRules: Hierarchy: K♦ is top. Then 'The Honors' (2♥, 4♣, 8♠, 9♥, 9♦). Then Aces, then Jacks, then Sixes (Póstarnir), then Eights (Friðurnar).
Rubbish: Kings (except K♦), Queens, and low numbers (2, 3, 4, 9 except honors) are 'rubbish'. They only win if everyone plays rubbish.
The Seven: If led, it cannot be beaten. If following, it beats nothing.
Múk: Taking the first 5 tricks scores 5 points.
Stroke: Taking 6-9 tricks in a row from the start scores points equal to the number of tricks.

strategy.basic: Save your 'Honors' (2♥, 4♣, etc.) to capture opponent High Cards. Don't waste your Sevens; they are your absolute weapons for leading when you are sure to win.
strategy.intermediate: If you have a terrible hand, use the 'Friðufær' rule to swap with the stock—it's often better than playing dead cards.
strategy.advanced: Coordinate with your partner's high card (shown at start). If your partner has the K♦, play defensively to let them win the lead, then protect their leads with rubbish.
tips: A Jack is often stronger than an Ace in this game because of the specific Karnöffel ordering.
Count the Eights. If they are gone, your Sixes (Póstarnir) become the masters of the board.

variations.name: Two-Player Alkort
variations.description: Identical rules but played as a duel. The stock exchange remains a vital element.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Two-player Alkort uses the same rules; no engine parameter overrides are required.

scoring.description: Points awarded at the end of each deal.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach a target point total (traditionally measured in stakes or 20-50 points).

synthesis.shortDescription: Discover the strangest ranking in card game history. In Alkort, a Seven is a god when led but a peasant when following. Master the 'Honor' cards and climb the 'Stroke' to victory.

hero.title: ALKORT
hero.subtitle: Ice and Iron Tricks
hero.tagline: An ancient guardian of the Icelandic card table.
